referred_to_by.content: A born-digital Metaconceptual Art work: a website built and owned by Sun & Rain Works around 2009, in connection with its Sotheby's Photographs auction engagement (sale N08533). Sun & Rain Works designates it as a work realising the concept of the auction as artwork.

www.wtfisart.com is associated by Sun & Rain Works with the concept of the auction as artwork, in which Sun & Rain Works designates its 2009 Sotheby's Photographs auction engagement as art. The designation is an assertion by the artist.

Sun & Rain Works reports domain-registration and hosting receipts, site metadata, and related records documenting the website's existence and date. The fuller archive remains held by the studio pending redaction and rights review.

referred_to_by._label: Evidence archive: the WTFIA source folder for www.wtfisart.com (2008-2009)

referred_to_by.content: What the public record of the domain shows, checked 2026-09-01. The Verisign registry gives wtfisart.com a registration event of 2024-08-29 under the handle 2912143398_DOMAIN_COM-VRSN, with nameservers at a shared hosting provider. A renewal does not reset a creation date, so a registration event of that date on a freshly issued handle means the domain lapsed at some earlier point and was registered again as a new object. The consequence is that the original creation date is no longer in the public registry and cannot be recovered from it. The Internet Archive holds no capture of the domain before 2011-02-10 21:34:22 UTC, which is its earliest; that capture is a parked advertising page carrying no studio content, which is what a registrar commonly serves at an address whose registration has lapsed, and it is therefore evidence about February 2011 rather than about 2009. Commercial historical-WHOIS services were not consulted: the free interfaces to them are gated behind human-verification challenges. The date the studio first registered this domain is therefore not recoverable from the registry, but it is no longer undetermined: the registrar's own receipts, described in the hosting-receipts record, give a registration of WTFISART.COM on 2009-03-16 at 00:45:06 UTC and hosting bought for it the same night, with that hosting paid monthly to at least 2009-12-15. Those are a third party's business records rather than the studio's assertion. What stood at the address in 2009 remains unevidenced.

The name reads two ways. Written without spaces or punctuation, wtfisart is both a question, 'WTF is art?', and a statement, 'WTF is art'. The studio holds, in its account given in 2026, that the double reading was deliberate and that registering the name declared the work art. The registrar's receipt of 2009-03-16, billed to Sun and Rain Works, independently dates the name; the intent is the studio's statement, and the hosting-receipts record sets out the distinction.

referred_to_by._label: Evidence archive: the registrar's receipts for the studio's domains (2009-2016)

referred_to_by.content: What the W stands for, in the artist's account. The studio states, in 2026, that the W of this work's name stands for 'What', so that it reads 'What the F is Art', while the W of the companion work WTF is Ansel Adams stands for 'Who'. No document from 2008 or 2009 spells out the expansion, and the reading is recorded as the artist's. It is consistent with the double reading recorded above: 'What' is the idiom's ordinary word, and the name is both the question what art is and the statement that it is that.

The work of the 2009 origin claim. This collection's origin claim for the 2009 engagement previously named a titled work, 'The Auction as Artwork', of which this website was modelled as an associated part. There was no such titled work, and the correction is set out in the record for the concept. The claim now names www.wtfisart.com, as the better dated of the studio's two works around the engagement: the registrar's receipt of 2009-03-16, billed to Sun and Rain Works, fixes the name fourteen days before the sale, on a document the studio did not write. WTF is Ansel Adams is recorded as the related work.
